problem_text:
A logistics firm must dispatch a technician to service five critical industrial sites:
Facility Alpha: Positioned at grid reference (48,47)
Facility Beta: Positioned at grid reference (8,156)
Facility Gamma: Positioned at grid reference (168,66)
Facility Delta: Positioned at grid reference (121,17)
Facility Epsilon: Positioned at grid reference (22,173)

The travel distances between sites, measured in kilometers, are pre-calculated as follows:
Alpha to Gamma: 121.5 km
Alpha to Delta: 78.9 km
Alpha to Epsilon: 128.7 km
Beta to Gamma: 183.6 km
Beta to Delta: 179.1 km
Beta to Epsilon: 22.0 km
Gamma to Delta: 67.9 km
Gamma to Epsilon: 181.0 km
Delta to Epsilon: 184.8 km

Direct transit between Facility Alpha and Facility Beta is impossible due to geographical barriers.
Furthermore, due to scheduling and permit restrictions, the route must incorporate exactly one of two specific connections: either the link between Facility Beta and Facility Gamma, or the link between Facility Gamma and Facility Delta.

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel circuit that services each facility precisely once, commencing and concluding at the same initial site.
